science.title: A New "Quasi-1D" State of Matter Could Be Hiding Inside Ice Giant Planets
science.description: Despite outward appearances, the internal workings of ice giants like Uranus and Neptune are extremely chaotic. Pressures millions of times greater than Earth’s sea level combine with temperatures in the thousands of degrees to make some pretty weird materials. Now, a new paper from researchers at the Carnegie Institution, published in Nature Communications, describes a completely new state of matter that might exist in these extreme environments - a “quasi-1D superionic” phase.

ai.description: A new perspective published in JAMA challenges the growing narrative that artificial intelligence (AI) is poised to replace physicians, arguing instead that the technology exposes deeper structural failures in modern health care. "This is not really a story about the end of the doctor," says Canio Martinelli, MD, OB/GYN, MSc, and lead author of the article. "It is a story about what kind of doctor, and what kind of medicine, we want to preserve and strengthen."
